1) Cell 1 shows numerous immunoglobulin genes (IGHG1, IGHG3, IGLV3-21, IGHGP, IGLL5, JCHAIN, etc.) along with MZB1, a known plasma cell marker, and JCHAIN (J chain) which is also highly characteristic of antibody-secreting plasma cells. This strongly indicates Cell 1 is a plasma cell.

2) Cell 9 expresses high levels of complement (C1QA, C1QB) and APOC1, alongside other macrophage-associated genes (e.g., FCER1G, which can be found in monocytes/macrophages), indicating an alveolar macrophage signature. Alveolar macrophages often express C1Q and apolipoproteins (APOC1, APOE), so Cell 9 is an alveolar macrophage.

3) Cell 4 is dominated by S100A8 and S100A9 and also has LYZ and AIF1 (IBA1), typical of myeloid cells, especially monocytes/neutrophils. The combination of S100A8 and S100A9 with LYZ strongly suggests a classical monocyte phenotype. Thus, Cell 4 is a classical monocyte.

4) Cell 5 has CD74 and HLA-DQB1 (in the top 50), pointing toward an antigen-presenting cell but without immunoglobulins. Since we have already assigned a monocyte and an alveolar macrophage, and B cells typically show immunoglobulin transcripts which are not seen here, the best match for Cell 5 is CD1c-positive myeloid dendritic cell.

5) Cell 3 includes TPPP3, AGR3, SLPI, and several cilia/secretory-associated or cilia-assembly genes (e.g., CAPS may be related, and the presence of TUBB4B). TPPP3 and AGR3 are known to be expressed in ciliated or secretory epithelial cells of the airway. This cluster of genes matches well with a ciliated columnar cell of the tracheobronchial tree.

Assigning Cell 8 as the conventional “B cell” is consistent, since plasma cell has already been used for Cell 1.

   – Cell 2 is almost entirely ribosomal/housekeeping genes without strong hints of antigen presentation or cilia/structure genes. T cells often show relatively modest top-gene diversity except for TCR/CD3 transcripts, which can be missed if overshadowed by housekeeping genes. Cell 2 is most plausibly the CD4-positive T cell.

7) Remaining for Cells 6, 7, and 10 are mast cell, respiratory basal cell, and capillary endothelial cell. <reasoning>1) First, note that there are exactly 10 cells and 10 candidate labels. Each label must be used once.

• CD1c-positive myeloid dendritic cell: Often expresses FCER1A, CD74, MHC class II genes.  
• CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell: May express T-cell markers (e.g. CD3E, CD52, CD8A/B), chemokines such as CCL5, and β2-microglobulin (B2M).  
• Capillary endothelial cell: Often expresses CLDN5, CAV1, ICAM1, and can have lower VWF than large-vessel endothelium.  
• Classical monocyte: Characteristically expresses high S100A8, S100A9, LYZ, and often TYROBP.  
• Elicited macrophage: Shares many myeloid markers (MAFB, APOE, C1QC, etc.) but tends to show more mature macrophage transcripts such as APOE, C1QC, and can co-express LYZ.  
• Nasal mucosa goblet cell: Typically expresses TFF3, other trefoil factors, and sometimes MUC genes; these are secretory epithelial cell markers.  
• Non-classical monocyte: Also myeloid, but without strong S100A8/A9. Often has MAFB, TYROBP, AIF1, FCER1G, etc., though not necessarily classical monocyte markers S100A8/A9.  
• Pulmonary alveolar type 2 cell: Typically expresses surfactant protein genes like SFTPB, SFTPD, etc.  
• Vein endothelial cell: Endothelial but often with higher VWF, VCAM1, E-selectin (SELE), ACKR1 compared to capillaries.

3) Match each cell:

Cell 4 strongly expresses S100A8, S100A9, and LYZ—hallmarks of classical monocytes.  

Cell 5 shows the surfactant protein SFTPB, indicating a pulmonary alveolar type 2 cell.  

Cell 6 expresses TFF3 (a goblet cell marker), consistent with nasal mucosa goblet cell.  

Cell 7 has APOE, C1QC, APOC1, LYZ, indicating a mature myeloid (macrophage-like) cell; best fits the elicited macrophage label.  

Cell 8 has FCER1A, CD74, HLA class II genes, typical of a myeloid dendritic cell (CD1c+).  

Cell 9 expresses CLDN5, CAV1, ICAM1, and other endothelial transcripts but lacks high VWF; fits capillary endothelial cell.  

Cell 10 has CD79A and IGLC2, which are immunoglobulin/B-cell markers, so it is a B cell.

   10) B cell</reasoning>

7) Capillary endothelial cell – often expresses CLDN5, KLF4, EPAS1, RGCC, and other endothelial‐associated markers.  
8) Ciliated columnar cell of tracheobronchial tree – may show secreted factors (e.g. SLPI) and sometimes coiled‐coil domain genes (CCDC*) associated with cilia.

5) Cell 3 shows high levels of FTL and FTH1 (ferritin light and heavy chains), CAPG (macrophage capping protein), and VIM (vimentin), consistent with an iron-laden myeloid phagocyte—typical of “alveolar macrophage.”

<reasoning>1) First, note that each of the ten candidate cell types must be used exactly once for the ten cells.

2) Cell 1 has high expression of TPPP3, CFAP53, RSPH1—genes typically associated with motile cilia—plus TPPP3 is well‐known as a ciliated epithelial marker. This strongly indicates a ciliated columnar cell of the tracheobronchial tree.

3) Cell 2 shows high APOC1, TYROBP, C1QA, plus heavy ferritin/light ferritin (FTH1, FTL), which is characteristic of alveolar macrophages (they often show APOC1, APOE, C1Q complex). 

4) Cell 3 has prominent S100A8 and S100A9—classical markers of “classical” monocytes (or sometimes neutrophils). The presence of SFTPC is likely background/ingested material rather than a genuine alveolar epithelial signature. Together with TMSB4X, FTH1, and moderate inflammatory genes, it aligns better with a classical monocyte identity.

5) Cell 4 strongly expresses cytotoxic/lytic molecules (GZMB, GNLY) and multiple chemokines (CCL3, CCL4, XCL2). Such a robust cytotoxic signature can be seen in either effector CD8 T cells or NK cells; however, XCL2 plus GZMB/GNLY at high levels is often found in strongly cytotoxic NK‐like populations. Assigning Cell 4 as the natural killer cell fits best in the global matching.

6) Cell 5 expresses numerous extracellular matrix/collagen‐associated genes (LUM, DCN, COL1A2, MFAP4, MGP) indicating a fibroblast lineage. The list calls it “alveolar type 1 fibroblast cell,” so Cell 5 is assigned accordingly.

7) Cell 6 contains TAGLN (transgelin) and other smooth muscle–associated transcripts, identifying it as tracheobronchial smooth muscle cell.

8) Among the remaining immune‐like cells, Cell 7 has a less “effector‐cytotoxic” signature and mostly ribosomal/housekeeping transcripts alongside a few general immune genes (SRGN, BTG1). This aligns more consistently with a CD4‐positive, alpha‐beta T cell that is not strongly cytotoxic.

9) Cell 8 expresses CCL4, TSC22D3 (GILZ), CXCR4, and other T‐cell–associated transcripts but lacks the strong GZMB/GNLY signature. An activated or memory‐biased CD8‐positive, alpha‐beta T cell is consistent here.

10) Cell 9 has key surfactant protein genes (SFTPC, SFTPB, SFTPA1, SFTPA2) that are hallmark markers of pulmonary alveolar type 2 cells.

11) Finally, Cell 10 expresses vascular adhesion genes (VCAM1, ICAM1, CLDN5) among others indicative of an endothelium—matching vein endothelial cell.

Putting it all together, each cell matches a unique candidate type:

5 → alveolar type 1 fibroblast cell  
6 → tracheobronchial smooth muscle cell  
7 → CD4‐positive, alpha‐beta T cell  
8 → CD8‐positive, alpha‐beta T cell  
9 → pulmonary alveolar type 2 cell  
10 → vein endothelial cell</reasoning>

<reasoning>I need to match each of the 10 cells (each from the same donor) to a unique one of the 10 listed cell types:  
• B cell  
• T cell  
• conventional dendritic cell  
• endothelial cell of lymphatic vessel  
• epithelial cell of lower respiratory tract  
• mast cell  
• pulmonary alveolar type 1 cell  
• pulmonary artery endothelial cell  
• respiratory basal cell  
• vein endothelial cell  

Below is the reasoning for each cell:

1) Cell 1 (top genes include CLDN5, PECAM1, ESAM, EFNB2). CLDN5, PECAM1 (CD31), ESAM, and EFNB2 are strongly associated with endothelial cells. EFNB2 in particular is known as an arterial endothelial marker. Thus Cell 1 matches “pulmonary artery endothelial cell.”

2) Cell 2 (top genes include HBB, HBA1/2, AGER, HOPX, KRT7, KRT19). The presence of AGER (RAGE) and HOPX is a classic signature of alveolar type 1 pneumocytes. Although hemoglobin gene expression (HBB, HBA) can appear due to ambient contamination, the key markers (AGER, HOPX) point to “pulmonary alveolar type 1 cell.”

3) Cell 3 (top genes include TPSB2, TPSAB1, CPA3). These are hallmark mast-cell tryptases (TPSAB1, TPSB2) and carboxypeptidase A3 (CPA3), which are specific to mast cells. Hence Cell 3 is “mast cell.”

4) Cell 4 (top genes include CCL5, IL32, CD52, plus many ribosomal proteins). CCL5 and IL32 are frequently associated with T cells, and CD52 is also highly expressed on lymphocytes (especially T cells). Therefore Cell 4 is “T cell.”

5) Cell 5 (top genes include CD74, CXCR4, with many ribosomal/translational genes). CD74 is the MHC class II chaperone, commonly found on antigen-presenting cells including B cells. A classic B-cell-specific transcript (e.g., MS4A1, CD79A) may not appear in the very top genes, but among the remaining unused immune cell types, B cell is the most consistent. Hence Cell 5 is “B cell.”

6) Cell 6 (top genes include CCL21, IGFBP7, and various ribosomal genes). CCL21 is a known chemokine strongly expressed by lymphatic endothelial cells. So Cell 6 is “endothelial cell of lymphatic vessel.”

7) Cell 7 (top genes include IGFBP7, SPARC, MGP). The overall endothelial signature suggests another endothelial cell, and having assigned artery (Cell 1) and lymphatic (Cell 6) already, this one corresponds to “vein endothelial cell.”

8) Cell 8 (top genes include KRT19, LAMB3, PKP3, TACSTD2, PERP). These are epithelial-structure genes often associated with basal cells (e.g., TACSTD2/Trop2, PKP3 in desmosomes). This fits “respiratory basal cell.”

9) Cell 9 (top genes include SCGB3A1, SCGB3A2, SLPI, SFTPB, SFTPA2). These are all secretory proteins characteristic of club cells / alveolar type 2 cells in the lung, but the matching category given is the broader “epithelial cell of lower respiratory tract.”

10) Cell 10 (top genes include CD74, CST3, LYZ, HLA-DRB5). MHC class II–associated molecules (CD74, HLA-DRB5) plus CST3 and LYZ are typical of myeloid or dendritic progeny. Since the only remaining unused myeloid category is “conventional dendritic cell,” Cell 10 must be “conventional dendritic cell.”

Hence the matches in order, Cells 1 through 10, are:  
1) pulmonary artery endothelial cell  
2) pulmonary alveolar type 1 cell  
3) mast cell  
4) T cell  
5) B cell  
6) endothelial cell of lymphatic vessel  
7) vein endothelial cell  
8) respiratory basal cell  
9) epithelial cell of lower respiratory tract  
10) conventional dendritic cell</reasoning>
